subject: science
passage: Oak trees do not produce the same number of acorns every autumn. In most years a forest's oaks drop only a modest crop, and then, every few years, nearly every tree in the region produces an enormous one, a pattern called masting. Ecologists have proposed that this boom-and-bust rhythm is a defense. <u>Squirrels, jays, and other seed eaters cannot multiply fast enough to consume a sudden glut of acorns, so in a mast year many seeds escape to sprout.</u> In lean years, meanwhile, the seed eaters' numbers fall, which makes the next glut even harder for them to exhaust. What signal keeps thousands of trees in step remains under investigation.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It presents an observation that contradicts the ecologists' proposal.
choices.B: It introduces the masting pattern that the text goes on to describe.
choices.C: It explains the reasoning behind the proposal stated in the previous sentence.
choices.D: It identifies the signal that causes oaks to mast in the same year.

explanation.why: The previous sentence says ecologists "have proposed that this boom-and-bust rhythm is a defense." The underlined sentence explains how that defense works: seed eaters cannot keep up with a glut, so many acorns survive. It supplies the logic behind the proposal.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The sentence supports the proposal rather than contradicting it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Masting is introduced in the first two sentences; the underlined sentence explains why it might be useful.
explanation.C: Correct. The sentence explains why a sudden glut of acorns works as a defense, which is the proposal made just before it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The final sentence says the signal "remains under investigation," so the text identifies no signal.
